routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas owns joinings of toral packets, measure rigidity for higher-rank torus actions, homogeneous Hecke sets or relative orbital integrals for (G^Δ, T^Δ): a catalogue-wide search for Duke-type equidistribution, measure rigidity, Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss, joinings, toral packets, Ratner and Linnik finds only GN.4, which schedules 'ergodic/mixing … proofs needed for Oppenheim/Duke-type arithmetic applications'. A Part II of GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic in GN.4's direction is right, and no other proposed Part II overlaps it. The review restated the brief's main theorem exactly: the extraction had dropped the bounded-conductor hypothesis f_i ≪ 1 and the archimedean condition g_∞^{-1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞ from Theorem 3.2 (preprint Theorem 14), and paraphrased its genericity condition. It also moved the brief to the published numbering and added nine items from the coverage check.

SV.0–SV.2 own sieve data, local densities, the Selberg and large sieves; the two-dimensional sieve for multiplicative functions along a binary polynomial (Theorem 9.7 and §9) and the local densities of Appendix B belong there. The review moved the local diagonalisation of a binary quadratic form (Lemma B.1) and the admissible lattice-point exponents (Definitions 10.8–10.9) to the parent roadmap's GN.2 and GN.4 (route 5), and added the statement that the ideal-counting function of an order lies in the class M(A,B,ε) (Proposition 10.10's proof).

HE.0 constructs quadratic orders, proper invertible ideals, Pic(O_c) and their comparison with idele-class quotients; the local and global orders of a homogeneous toral set and Appendix A's principal genus theory for an arbitrary order are statements about exactly those objects. The review added the identification of a packet's class group with Pic(Λ), Corollary A.7 and Proposition A.11. For maximal orders, Tau Ceti Multiquadratic layer 3 already plans the genus-field description of Cl/Cl²; the non-maximal statements remain HE.0's.

AA.4 plans strong approximation, from which the finite abelian quotient G_res and the components of the arithmetic quotient come. The review added item 8 (the reduced-norm description of G(A)/G(A)^+), which the extraction had marked planned but which no stage states.

Added by the review: GN.2 owns the local classification of quadratic forms including the dyadic case, and GN.4 lattice-point estimates for convex bodies; the two items moved here from route 2 are statements of those kinds.

notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026. The extraction read arXiv v3; the review read the published article (Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 145–276) in full from the journal's free PDF and matched every item to it. Locators now give the published section, number and page, with the preprint number in parentheses (the Annals edition renumbers by section; no statement changed between v3 and print). 59 item statements were corrected (missing hypotheses, wrong value sets, garbled formulas; the main theorem's bounded-conductor hypothesis), 13 items were added from a coverage check of the published text, and item 8 was moved from planned to missing. The three source issues were confirmed in print (E2 occurs five times, not three), and 31 further mistakes were found and checked on page images, among them errors in Appendix B's local densities (Lemma B.4, Proposition B.5, Corollary B.7, checked by direct counts), the false inequality 2κ|D| ≤ A(E) in the proof of Proposition 10.10 (repaired by rescaling η), the error term |D|^{-2/3} for |D|^{-1/3} in Proposition 10.14, a gap in range R_2 of the proof of Theorem 9.7 (Q = x² violates the needed uniform bound), and the wrong definition of O_∞^×. None affects the main theorems. Every change is listed in research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19.md.
